chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ibn Abi Umayr from 'Umar ibn Udhaynah from 'Ali ibn Sa'id al-Basri said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): I am staying among the Banu 'Adi, and their muezzin and their imam and all the people of the mosque are Uthmaniyyah, who disown you and your Shī'ah, and I am staying among them. So what do you think regarding prayer behind the imam?

He said: 'And count it as reward for what you hear, and if you came to al-Basrah, al-Fudayl ibn Yasar would ask you, and you would tell him what I gave you as a ruling, so you would take al-Fudayl's opinion and leave my opinion.'

'Ali said: So I came to al-Basrah and informed al-Fudayl of what he said, so he said: 'He (the Imam) knows better what he said, but I have heard him and I heard his father saying: Do not count the prayer behind the Nāsib (one who opposes the Ahl al-Bayt), and read for yourself as if you are alone.'
He said: So I took al-Fudayl's opinion and left the opinion of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him).

key_terms.اَلنَّاصِبِ: The Nāsib, one who opposes or is hostile to the Ahl al-Bayt
key_terms.اَلْفُضَيْلُ بْنُ يَسَارٍ: Al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, a prominent companion of the Imams
key_terms.اِحْتَسِبْ: Count it as reward or consider it valid
key_terms.عُثْمَانِيَّةٌ: Uthmaniyyah, a group known for their loyalty to Caliph Uthman and opposition to the Ahl al-Bayt

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on praying behind an imam who opposes the Ahl al-Bayt according to this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith illustrates the Shia jurisprudential principle of *al-istihna'* (disregarding the validity of the prayer) when praying behind a *Nāsib* (one who opposes the Ahl al-Bayt), contrasting it with the more lenient view of counting the prayer as valid. It highlights the dynamic between the Imam’s direct authority and the scholarly consensus of his companions, specifically al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, whose opinion the narrator ultimately adopted for practical consistency. The narrative underscores the importance of recognizing the spiritual status of the imam in determining the completeness of the congregational prayer.
